answer: A sponsor carries 68% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the grove liability is entered in the wharf ledger at admission, the meadow audit reveals the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must thus place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 25 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
